pass_a_gloss: But the God of all, if he should wish to do something, what would be the thing standing against and leading out against it? For what God the holy wills, who will scatter? And the high hand, who will turn back? So for proof that he is God by nature and truly, the 'All my counsel will stand, and all things as many as I have counselled I will do' would fittingly be said by him. Then besides this he says: Calling from the east a bird, and from a land far off, about the things I have counselled; and the 'I am' will follow this too. And the bird called from the east and from a land far off we say is the Babylonian, who, having burned the whole country of the Jews, took Jerusalem and shook down the temple in it; then having uprooted very many of both the common and the notable, he carried them away from the land that bore them, and deposited them in the country and land of the Persians, having thrown upon them hard and unbearably the yoke of the captivity. And this too will be clear to you, from the things which God said to the blessed prophet Ezekiel. And it runs thus: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, narrate a narration, and speak a parable to the house of Israel, and you will say: Thus says Adonai Lord: The great eagle, long in stretching, full of talons, which has the leading to enter into Lebanon, and took the choice of the cedar, nipped off the tops of the tenderness, and brought them into land of Canaan, into a walled city he set them, and took from the seed of the land, and gave it into the plain as a plant, in much water, he set it being watched over, and it became into a weak vine, and small in the size, so that its branches appear toward him, and its roots were under its land. And it became into a vine, and made shoots, and stretched out its climbing. These things then God said to the blessed prophet Ezekiel. And since the word was hard to reach, and the force of the thoughts not very clear to the hearers, he himself makes it plain again, saying: And say to the house of Israel, the provoking one: Do you not know what these things are which I said? When the king of Babylon comes upon Jerusalem, he will also take its king and its rulers, and will lead them to himself into Babylon. And he will take from the seed of the kingdom, and will covenant with him a covenant, and will bring him in under a curse, and will take the leaders of the land, for the kingdom to become weak, and not to be lifted up at all, to keep his covenant and to make it stand. pass_b_english: But if the God of all wishes to do anything, what could there be to stand against it and oppose it? For “what the holy God wills, who will scatter? And His high hand, who will turn it back?” (Isaiah 14:27). So, as proof that He is God by nature and in truth, He may fittingly say: “All My counsel will stand, and all that I have planned I will do” (Isaiah 46:10). Then He adds to this: “calling a bird from the east, and from a land far off, for the things I have planned” (Isaiah 46:11); and to this also the words “I am” will be joined.

The bird called from the east and from a land far off we say is the Babylonian, who set fire to the whole country of the Jews, took Jerusalem and shook down the temple in it. Then, uprooting very many of both the common people and the notable, he carried them away from their native land and settled them in the country and land of the Persians, laying on them the hard and unbearable yoke of captivity. This too will be clear to you from what God said to the blessed prophet Ezekiel. It runs thus:

“And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, tell a tale and speak a parable to the house of Israel, and say: Thus says Adonai, the Lord: The great eagle, of great span, full of talons, whose purpose is to enter Lebanon, took the choice parts of the cedar; he nipped off the tops of its tender shoots and brought them into the land of Canaan; he set them in a walled city. And he took some of the seed of the land and put it in the plain as a plant beside much water; he set it where it could be watched over. And it became a weak vine, small in size, so that its branches showed toward him, and its roots were beneath it in its ground. And it became a vine, and put out shoots, and stretched out its climbing branches” (Ezekiel 17:1-6).

These things God said to the blessed prophet Ezekiel. But since the saying was hard to grasp and the force of its meaning not very clear to the hearers, He Himself explains it again, saying: “Say to the rebellious house of Israel: Do you not know what these things are that I have said? When the king of Babylon comes against Jerusalem, he will take its king and its rulers and lead them to himself into Babylon. And he will take one of the royal seed, and make a covenant with him, and bring him under a curse; and he will take the leaders of the land, so that the kingdom may become weak and never lift itself up, but keep his covenant and uphold it” (Ezekiel 17:12-14).

choices.term: Ἃ γὰρ Θεὸς ὁ ἅγιος βούλεται, τίς διασκεδάσει;
choices.english: what the holy God wills, who will scatter?
choices.why: The quotation is Isaiah 14:27, set before Isaiah 46:10.
Isaiah 46:10 is spoken by God, as proof of his godhead; it is not said about him.

choices.english: settled them in the country and land of the Persians
choices.why: The deportation to the land of the Persians is kept.
The opening formula of the Ezekiel quotation is kept.
δυσέφικτος, hard to reach; the parable needed God's own explanation.
